page: Amazon Web Services c5ad.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor running at 3.3 GHz. It features 4 vCPUs (2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled) and 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The instance is built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and includes 150 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage, alongside a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate a mixed performance profile. Single-core performance is moderate, with Geekbench single-core and single-threaded gzip compression scoring in the average range. However, multi-core and memory-bound operations show limitations; stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Passmark memory scores fall into the bottom 10%, while Geekbench multi-core and software compilation benchmarks register in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with read and write speeds categorized as weak.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c5ad.xlarge offers dedicated AMD EPYC compute resources paired with fast local NVMe SSD storage, making it a viable option for workloads requiring temporary high-speed storage without the overhead of network-attached volumes. However, the lower memory density and weak multi-core scaling present tradeoffs for resource-intensive applications. This instance is best suited for light compute tasks, single-threaded processing, basic web serving, and development workloads that benefit from local scratch space.
